title: How the farm reads through the walls
question:
**The design changed under this card on 2026-09-15 and the question got smaller.**

P-18 now reads: one world, one metric, two grids. A building's interior is a finer grid nested inside the building's own footprint — the house stands on 3 tiles by 2, the room inside is 6 cells by 3 at half that pitch, which is 3 tiles by 1.5 and fits, with the top half-row left for the roof. Going inside is a uniform camera zoom of x2 and nothing else. Nothing stretches, nothing is registered to anything, because nothing ever comes apart.

The attached panels are that: the same photograph of the running game, the same composition, one zoom between them.

So the geometric question this card used to ask — registered to the doorway, or a backdrop lining up with nothing — is gone. There is no lie to catch. What is left is **grain**: at x2 the yard is drawn at six screen pixels per art pixel, and whether that reads as *outside, seen through a window* or as *the world came closer* is a matter of treatment.

On an 800x600 screen at camera scale 3 the room fills 288x144 and there are 2.7 tiles of yard across and 3.2 down — the hen, the shipping bin, the fence and the neighbour's plot all read. That is a real amount of farm, and it is worth deciding how much you want to see of it.
why_now: The geometry is settled and this is what is left of how it looks. It is cheap to try - all four are a shader or a dither over one layer - and it wants captures rather than paragraphs, which is a day's work once one room is playable.

options.label: Nothing at all
options.detail: Draw the yard exactly as it is drawn outdoors, only twice the size. Honest and free. The risk is that indoors and outdoors look like the same place at different zooms, which is what they are, and nothing says 'you are inside'.

options.label: Haze
options.detail: An ordered dither of one pale colour over everything beyond the walls, on the art's own pixel grid — the studio's existing vocabulary for a soft edge, no blur. Says 'through a window' without hiding the hen.

options.label: Desaturate and darken
options.detail: Keep every pixel but drain the yard towards grey and down a step in value, so the room is the lit thing. Reads as an interior most strongly; the price is that a crow out there is harder to notice, which is one of the reasons for seeing out.

options.label: Hard-cut walls, clear yard
options.detail: No treatment on the yard at all, but the walls draw as a solid opaque frame that bites into it, so what you see out is framed rather than faded. The window metaphor made literal; costs wall art the game does not have yet.

links.label: The chapter this comes from (design/15, Interiors)

attachments.caption: The two zooms. Left: the house on its three tiles by two, the room inside at half pitch. Right: x2, and nothing has moved. Both the same photograph of the game.
